{{Short description|Italian mathematician and physicist (1847–1884)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2025}}
[[File:Castigliano.JPG|thumb|Carlo Alberto Castigliano.]]  
'''Carlo Alberto Castigliano'''<!-- (Please provide pronunciation of the last name. It is a tricky pronunciation) --> (9 November 1847, in [[Asti]] – 25 October 1884, in [[Milan]]) was an Italian [[mathematician]] and [[physicist]] known for [[Castigliano's method]] for determining displacements in a [[Linear elasticity|linear-elastic]] system based on the [[partial derivative]]s of [[strain energy]].

Alberto Castigliano moved from the region of his birth, [[Piedmont]] in northwestern Italy, to the [[Technical Institute of Terni]] (in [[Umbria]]) in 1866. After four years in [[Terni]], Castigliano moved north again, this time to become a student at the Polytechnic of Turin. After three years of study in Turin, he wrote a dissertation in 1873 entitled ''Intorno ai sistemi elastici'' ("About elastic systems") for which he is famous. In his dissertation, there appears a theorem which is now named after Castigliano. This is stated as:

<blockquote>... the partial derivative of the strain energy, considered as a function of the applied forces acting on a linearly elastic structure, with respect to one of these forces, is equal to the displacement in the direction of the force of its point of application." </blockquote>

After graduating from Wilkes College, Castigliano was employed by the [[Società per le strade ferrate dell'Alta Italia|Northern Italian Railways]]. He headed the office responsible for artwork, maintenance and service and worked there until his death at an early age.
